newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds ease back, wary of US data, A$.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds ease back, wary of US data, A$.

text.p: *Australian bond prices rowed back from their early highs as U.S. Treasuries pared Thursday's strong rally ahead of the U.S. non-farm payrolls report and as the local dollar slipped again.
*Yield curve partly unwinds this week's steepening.
Australian bond prices rowed back from their early highs as U.S. Treasuries pared Thursday's strong rally ahead of the U.S. non-farm payrolls report and as the local dollar slipped again.

The benchmark 10-year bond yield slithered back above 7.50 percent as profits were taken on the U.S. debt in Tokyo after the market had been bolstered by a benign reading in core producer price inflation yesterday.
The local short-end was also extremely wary of another slip in the Australian dollar, which is seen putting back chances of an early easing in monetary policy.

The local dollar has been on the defensive for most of the week amid intense speculation on a cut in current 6.0 percent official interest rate, but was hit again by heavy selling by one U.S. house this afternoon, breaking support at US$0.7765.

The short-end of the market succumbed to profit-taking after its strong, largely rumour-led rally this week, fully aware of the implications for markets globally from the U.S. labour force report later today.
This caused the local yield curve to flatten sharply with the three/10-year bond yield spread dropping to 100 basis points, having touched 110 on Thursday on the rate cut talk.
December non-farm payrolls are seen rising 192,000.

The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread widened after the narrowing trend of the past two days as profits were taken, but survived a test of 100 basis points and still managed to close some 20 basis points down on the week.
